What specific activities or sensations trigger this shooting ear pain since your tympanoplasty?

Please describe any changes in hearing or tinnitus you have experienced.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-tympanoplasty neuralgia (glossopharyngeal or trigeminal nerve entrapment) likely due to graft tension or neuroma, unrelated to tuberculosis. The shooting pain with eating (triggered by the stylopharyngeus muscle) and earring discomfort (touching the auricle) are classic signs of nerve hypersensitivity after middle ear surgery, not an infectious process like TB. Let's proceed with a focused ENT exam to check for graft retraction or granulation tissue before considering a nerve block.
